title: Free night offsets retain 15 percent of the WASP-105 candidate amplitude information in a circular giant model
abstract: We test the part of the 2.0028-day WASP-105 candidate velocity signal that survives free offsets for each observing night. We use 21 archival HARPS measurements on 12 nights after removal of the known giant planet transit. With a circular giant model and a linear trend, free night offsets retain 15.04 percent of the amplitude information in a one-offset fit. The signed amplitude changes from 8.03 plus or minus 3.00 to -5.25 plus or minus 7.75 m/s under fixed Gaussian photon errors. Detection power for a true 5 m/s amplitude falls to 4.64 percent at a one-sided 1 percent test threshold. Extra giant harmonics raise the free-night error to 110.92 m/s, but are not a physical eccentric orbit fit. Exact projection, direct fit checks and 100,000 Gaussian trials support the conditional calculation. They do not test real stellar noise. This extends a prior finite nightly-noise test with the same data. No new planet, mass detection, host identification or independent observing confirmation is found.

display.caption: Fixed nightly-error scenarios, exact free-night limits and conditional Gaussian detection power. The circular giant model retains 15.04 percent of the one-offset amplitude information.

citations.reason: Tests the exact free-night limit of its archival velocity analysis.
